<div class="site-note credits-note">
<p><strong>Greek text.</strong> <i>Epicteti dissertationes ab Arriano digestae</i>, editio maior, edited by Heinrich Schenkl, Leipzig, Teubner, 1916. Taken from the <a href="https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/">Perseus Digital Library</a> (Tufts University), URN <code>urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0557.tlg001.perseus-grc2</code>.</p>
<p><strong>English translation.</strong> George Long, <i>The Discourses of Epictetus, with the Encheiridion and Fragments</i>, London, George Bell and Sons, 1890. Taken from the <a href="https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/">Perseus Digital Library</a>, URN <code>urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0557.tlg001.perseus-eng3</code>. The footnotes are Long&#x27;s own and are printed in full at the end of each discourse.</p>
